newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - Reuters foreign exchange poll - Oct.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Reuters foreign exchange poll - Oct.

text.p: The dollar is expected to fall from current levels against the yen over the next month and is expected to continue its retreat over the next year, according to a Reuter poll of 35 banks and financial institutions across the globe, conducted on October 3 and 4.

At 1040 GMT, the dollar was trading at 1.5305/10 marks and 111.50/60 yen. Sterling/dollar was quoted at $1.5648/55, sterling/mark at 2.3955/60 and mark/yen at 72.83/86.
The minimum and maximum forecasts were as follows --

On average, forecasters expect sterling to be trading at $1.5639 in one months time, slightly off current levels, before continuing its decline to $1.5408 in six months time. It is then expected to pickup to $1.5452 a year from now. The lowest sterling is expected to fall is to $1.4100 over the next twelve months. The maximum level it is predicted to climb to is $1.6320 during the same period.

Against the mark, the U.S currency is expected to make some progress with forecasters predicting it to trade at 1.5386 marks in three months time. It is then expected to fall to 1.5363 in six months before accelerating its decline to 1.5173 in twelve months. The lowest dollar/mark prediction for this period is 1.4200 marks, and the highest is 1.7000.

The dollar is expected to fall against the yen during the months ahead, slipping to 107.55 in twelve months time. En route, it is expected to trade at 110.80 in three months and 109.70 in six months time. The highest forecast for dollar/yen during this period is 120.00 yen, and the lowest is 98.00.
Rankings of the 35 forecasters by the accuracy of their one-month forecasts will be published in the first week of November just before the results of the next poll.
